entities.name: --report
entities.description: A render report feature that currently says 'peak 0.900' without distinguishing how much of the signal sits at the ceiling.

entities.name: Ceiling share item
entities.description: Item 1: the idea that --report should show a ceiling: X% line since peak alone can't distinguish mixes with very different amounts of limiting.

entities.name: Pitch content item
entities.description: Item 2: the idea for a per-bar score report (banks, note counts, pitch-class sets) so a blind/textual reader can know what harmony sounds, not just edit it.

entities.name: doc/trial/spelling-preference.md
entities.description: A 2026-09-05 trial that gave eight arms MIDI-number material and asked for the harmony described, answering part of item 2 by showing note names are wanted.

entities.name: tools/modecheck.py
entities.description: Tool whose places_to_rest function already collects sounding pitches per bar across banks and reduces them to one number, covering part of item 2's need.

entities.name: places_to_rest
entities.description: A function in tools/modecheck.py that collects per-bar sounding pitches across banks and reduces them to a single number, discarding most of what item 2 wants.

entities.name: scoreLead
entities.description: A tool/checker whose rule that equations must be adjacent was broken by placing a #: comment between equations of one name.

entities.name: Comment-splits-equation item
entities.description: Item 3: whether a #: doc comment should be allowed to live between equations of one name, a taste question raised when it broke scoreLead.

entities.name: drive
entities.description: A synth parameter whose amount 1.4 yields a 13.6x input gain, a scale surprise learned only from synth.ges source at the cost of a flattened render.

entities.name: synth.ges
entities.description: Source file from which drive's true gain scale had to be learned, at the cost of one whole render flattened.

entities.name: Drive scale-surprise item
entities.description: Item 4: the proposal to add a #: try: line at drive's use site noting that 0.2 is already a crunch.

entities.name: Memory-index gate item
entities.description: Item 5: the observation that the memory-index gate skips itself silently under the sandbox, so a broken gate can go unclaimed on the very machine it guards.

entities.name: test_memoryindex.py
entities.description: A test that skips silently when run in a sandbox unable to see ~/.claude, hiding the memory-index gate's failure.

entities.name: tools/memoryindex.py
entities.description: The memory-index tool observed on 2026-08-29 reporting 'no index' for a file that existed.

entities.name: Two-writers rule
entities.description: A rule about two writers in one file that met music for the first time on 2026-08-29, requiring that one hand's change must never drown silently.

relations.description: Henri asked for ideas after a day of music-making, prompting this card's creation and batching by his word.
The piece and day that generated the five marks documented in this card.
The card records what a full day of using gestate as a musician left behind.
Item 2 of this card is kin to drawn-scores.md's constraint about textual projection for hearing.
Records the same day's larger verdict, kept separately from this card's five items.
Item 5 is defect-shaped and belongs in fixme.md with an F-number when taken up.
The proposed ceiling: X% report line would put this test's headroom criterion into every run's own output.
Item 1 proposes adding a ceiling share line to the --report output.
Item 2 is kin to drawn-scores.md's constraint that a textual being needs a textual projection for hearing.
The trial answered part of item 2 by showing that eight of eight arms wrote the pitch report using note names.
Gave arms MIDI-number material from this section and asked for the harmony described, confirming the need for note-name output.
modecheck.py's places_to_rest already collects most of the per-bar pitch data item 2 asks for.
places_to_rest is a function within tools/modecheck.py that reduces sounding pitches per bar to one number.
Placing a #: comment between equations of one name broke scoreLead's adjacency rule.
Item 4 concerns drive's scale surprises, where amount 1.4 yields 13.6x input gain.
The true gain scale of drive was learned only from synth.ges source, costing a flattened render.
Item 5 concerns test_memoryindex.py silently skipping under a sandbox that cannot see ~/.claude.
The gate reported 'no index' for an existing file, the seen failure behind item 5.
The day's two-writer editing observation, recorded as this card's non-ask item, met music for the first time.
If the duet format in drawn-scores.md is tried, it inherits the two-writers rule that one hand's change must never drown silently.
Henri was one of the two writers whose values survived the session's loudly-failing edit.
